CHIEF COMPLAINT
Asthma exacerbated by sports activity and concerns about mood.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a young athlete who reports difficulty with asthma that worsens with aerobic activity, particularly water polo. Symptoms typically occur during or after physical exertion and include phlegm buildup in the throat, coughing, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness. Patient uses albuterol inhaler (2 puffs) as needed, which helps alleviate symptoms but still requires sitting down to recover; recovery typically occurs within 15 minutes. Patient reports tremor/shakiness after using inhaler. Additionally reports mild coughing when around smoke. Denies nocturnal awakenings due to asthma. Currently not on any daily asthma medications. Symptoms occur with virtually every aerobic workout. Patient also reports recent mood changes including increased stress, sadness, lack of motivation, social withdrawal, and fatigue. Patient attributes mood changes to pressure from upcoming SATs, AP classes, and general academic stress. Mood changes began at the start of the school year. Denies difficulty with focusing or information retention, but reports feeling down and not wanting to do activities that friends suggest.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reports seasonal allergies. No nocturnal asthma symptoms. No other systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler as needed (2 puffs during acute symptoms).

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies noted.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Student with academic responsibilities including SAT preparation and AP classes. Participates in water polo. Reports stress related to academic expectations.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
General: Alert and cooperative.
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
HEENT: Eyes normal, ears show mild fluid bilaterally, throat normal, no tonsillar abnormalities.
Abdomen: Bowel sounds normal, no tenderness or masses on palpation.
Neurological: Reflexes normal and symmetric.

RESULTS
Mild fluid noted in both ears. Seasonal allergies suspected.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma, exercise-induced: Start daily montelukast (Singulair) for asthma control given suspected underlying allergic component. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed for acute symptoms. Tremor is expected side effect of albuterol; reassured patient. Follow-up in 6 weeks to assess response to daily medication.
2. Mood concerns/depression: Referred to therapist for evaluation and ongoing care. Screening questionnaires to be completed. Follow-up in 2 weeks to review results and discuss progress.
